sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Carve — Dealing physical damage to champions reduces the target's Armor by 6% for 6 seconds. (stacks 5 times).
values [6.0, 5.0, 6.0, 30.0, 5.0] with units [s, flat, percent, percent, s] — 6 s duration, 5 stacks, 6% per stack, 30% cap

…deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} bonus physical damage on-hit. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources — i.e. Bloodsong contributes a damage AMP, never an armor_reduction_percent row; the only percent-armor-reduction source named in this scenario is the Black Cleaver.

reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct): R ← R − r_flat; R ← R·(1 − r_pct/100) … apply_{armor,magic}_penetration(R, f, p): R ← max(0, R·(1 − p) − f). Reduction is target-side (it can push resistance negative); penetration is attacker-personal and floors at 0.
The stack *duration* (6 s) is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic AS·u > 1/6, so expiry does not rescue the constant…

F3 shred-first: E (Roar of the Slayer, 25% armor reduction) … mitigates at Ahri's shredded armor 92 x 0.75 = 69 → 676.4 x 100/169 = 400.2 — the repo's own convention for a percent armor reduction row (multiply armor by (1 − fraction), then mitigate with 100/(100+R)).

The engine has derive_ally_effects / support entries (support_effects.py, item_support_effects.py) — i.e. the `support_*` ledger is the ally/utility-effect layer, which is exactly where a team-wide target debuff granted by a roster member belongs.

step_1_max_carve_fraction.note: matches the cached wiki branch and the Riot description verbatim; the atom row carries the same [6% per stack, 5 stacks, 30% cap, 6 s] tuple

step_2_is_the_row_legitimate_at_all.rule: Carve is written as a debuff ON THE TARGET ("reduces the target's Armor by 6%"), not as personal penetration. Per docs/math-foundations.md §2.2 the engine models reduction target-side (reduce_resistance) and penetration attacker-side (apply_*_penetration). A target-side armor reduction therefore lowers the target's armor for EVERY damage source in the roster, including allies — so a `support_resistance_reduction` (ally/utility-layer) row carrying `Black Cleaver — Carve` is the game-correct way to express the Cleaver's contribution to a coupled roster fight.
step_2_is_the_row_legitimate_at_all.cross_check: Bloodsong, the scenario's other named item, grants Expose Weakness (8%/5% increased damage taken) — a damage amp, not an armor_reduction_percent. So the Cleaver row is the only percent-armor-reduction the scenario can produce; deleting it deletes the scenario's own subject.

step_3_factor_reconstruction.definition_inferred: factor = physical-damage amplification produced by the shred = m(R·(1−f)) / m(R) with m(R) = 100/(100+R) (docs/math-foundations.md §2.1)
step_3_factor_reconstruction.plausibility: level-18 armor of a front-line target lands right there (Malphite 124.15 → 1.1993, Hecarim 124.65 → 1.1997, Darius 125.40 → 1.2003, Sejuani 126.65 → 1.2014), so `factor: 1.2` is the correctly rounded amplification for a 30% Carve against a ~125-armor target
step_3_factor_reconstruction.conclusion: the old row's two numbers are mutually consistent AND consistent with the cached wiki text — 0.3 is the sourced 5-stack cap, 1.2 is the exact 100/(100+R) amplification it produces

step_4_can_the_absence_be_correct.expiry_check: Carve lasts 6 s and refreshes on every physical-damage instance; docs/math-foundations.md §2.3 states the 6 s duration is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic attack speed. Event index 46 is deep into the fight, where an in-game Carve is unambiguously at the 5-stack cap. Neither ramp-up (a late event is past the ramp) nor expiry (duration ≫ swing interval) can explain the row vanishing at event 46.
step_4_can_the_absence_be_correct.stack_cap_check: 0.3 is the cap, not an over-application: no reading of the cached text yields more than 30%.
step_4_can_the_absence_be_correct.residual_uncertainty: The one rule that WOULD justify deletion is de-duplication: Carve stacks live on the target and cap at 30% total, so the same debuff must be counted exactly once. If `support_resistance_reduction[0..3]` already contained an identical `Black Cleaver — Carve` row (a second Cleaver holder, or the attacker's own Cleaver leaking into the ally layer), then removing the duplicate would be correct and the composed shred would be unchanged. Deciding that requires the sibling array elements, which live in scripts/golden_baseline.json — outside the permitted evidence tree. On the evidence available (data/ + docs/math-foundations.md) there is no rule that makes a fully-stacked Carve stop reducing the target's armor for a roster participant at a late event.

computed_correct_value.derivation: 5 stacks × 6% = 30% target armor reduction (cached wiki + Riot text); 125 armor → 87.5 → 100/187.5 ÷ 100/225 = 1.2× physical damage

verdict_rationale: The removed row reproduces exactly from the cached sources: 6% × 5 stacks = 30% armor reduction (fraction 0.3), and that shred yields a 1.2× physical-damage factor against a ~125-armor target under m(R) = 100/(100+R). Black Cleaver's Carve is a target-side debuff ("reduces the target's Armor"), so it belongs in the ally/utility (`support_*`) reduction ledger of a coupled roster fight, and at event 46 — late in the fight, with a 6 s refresh window longer than the inter-swing interval — it is at max stacks and cannot have expired. Dropping the row understates physical damage against the target by the full 1.2× amplification. Caveat recorded above: if the same list already carried an identical Carve row, the deletion would instead be a correct de-duplication; that check needs scripts/golden_baseline.json, which this oracle is barred from reading.
